Goal: A full creative and game-feel audit of this project, producing a
prioritized, categorized backlog of design improvements — not code changes,
not one feature, a design document I can react to and then feed into /idea
one item at a time.

Do not interrogate me with clarifying questions before starting. I don't have
strong opinions yet on how this genre of game should look and feel — that's
the point of this audit. Read the actual codebase, any existing plan
documents, README, and git history to ground every recommendation in what
this project actually is, then use your own judgment about what "good" looks
like for a top-down, conversation-driven, LLM-NPC town game specifically —
not generic game-polish advice that could apply to anything.

Cover, as separate sections:
1. Visual style and art direction — cohesion, what's currently placeholder
   vs. intentional, what a stronger visual identity would look like given
   the existing size-contract and socket systems already in place.
2. Game feel / "juice" — feedback on player actions, animation weight,
   camera behavior, UI responsiveness — the small polish details that
   separate "functional" from "satisfying" in this genre.
3. UX and menu/dialogue flow — is the conversation interface actually
   pleasant to use repeatedly, given that talking to NPCs is the core loop
   here, not a side activity.
4. Pacing and progression — what makes a town worth continuing to explore
   past the first ten minutes; reference how other conversation-driven or
   town-sim games handle this, and name what you're drawing on.
5. Atmosphere and narrative texture — environmental storytelling,
   ambient detail, anything that makes the world feel authored rather than
   assembled.

For each recommendation: state what's true now, what you'd change, why it
matters specifically for THIS game (not a generic best-practice), and how
it's sized (S/M/L) so I can gauge effort before committing to it.

Be honest and specific rather than diplomatically vague — if something is
currently weak, say so plainly. I'd rather get a real assessment than a
softened one.

Goal: Fix gun aim direction, add more character style variety, and replace
the character-creator preview's auto-spin with player-driven rotation that
falls back to facing the player after real inactivity.

Context:
1. Gun aim likely has the same root cause as the earlier moonwalk fix —
   aim direction is stored/updated somewhere separate from the actual
   aim target (cursor position, look vector, whatever drives it), so the
   two have drifted out of sync. Apply the same fix pattern: derive aim
   direction from the authoritative target every frame rather than storing
   it independently. Do not patch this per-weapon or per-animation-state;
   fix it at the source the same way facing was fixed.
2. More character styles — extend the existing socket/style-tag system
   (heads, eyes, hair, body, etc.) with additional style-tagged part sets.
   No new architecture needed here; this should be additive within the
   existing contract, not a parallel system.
3. Character-creator preview currently auto-spins continuously on an
   internal timer, forcing the player to wait out a full rotation to see
   details like the eyes. Replace this entirely:
   - Rotation is driven only by player drag/input while input is active.
   - A time-since-last-input counter tracks inactivity.
   - Only after a defined idle timeout (not immediately) does the model
     ease toward a fixed default orientation — facing the player/camera —
     rather than continuing any spin.
   - There should be no code path where an autonomous spin runs
     unconditionally; input and idle-fallback are the only two states.
   - If an auto-rotate "preview mode" is wanted later, that's a separate,
     explicitly opt-in third state — do not build it now, just don't
     structure the fix in a way that makes it hard to add later.

Mii/Tomodachi-Life-inspired look, expand character customization variety, add
playable-character (not just NPC) look customization, and have Claude actively
playtest the result to surface further improvement ideas.

Context: This builds on existing systems already in place — the size-contract
(entity world size independent of sprite pixel dimensions) and the socket/
attach-point system for compositional character parts. The art style overhaul
and expanded customization should be built as extensions of these systems,
not parallel ones.

Scope:

PART A — Engine assessment (recommendation only, do not execute)
- Assess whether the current rendering/engine setup can reasonably support a
  cohesive cartoony, Mii-style visual target, or whether it's a genuine
  blocker.
- If a migration looks warranted: do NOT start migrating. Instead produce a
  written recommendation with reasoning, and a migration plan document
  (scope, risk, rough sequencing) saved to .claude/plans/, for me to review
  and decide on manually. This is a hard stop — a full engine migration is
  too large and risky to execute unattended overnight.
- If no migration is needed: state that plainly and move to Part B.

PART B — Art style overhaul (proceed regardless of Part A's outcome, scoped
to what's achievable within the current engine)
- Move the visual direction toward cartoony/Mii-style: simplified,
  friendly proportions, clean bold outlines, a cohesive color palette —
  reference Tomodachi Life and Mii-style character design as the concrete
  target, not vague "cuter" language.
- Apply consistently across roaming NPCs, the character creator's parts
  pool, and the player's own avatar — all three must draw from the same
  shared parts library (per the earlier pool-unification fix), so this
  doesn't reintroduce a mismatch between them.
- Leave a clear seam for swapping in purchased/downloaded graphics packs
  later — style should be a tagged property on parts, not hardcoded
  assumptions baked into rendering logic.

Goal: A trait system for NPC personalities — traits are data (behavior
rules + example lines) composed into the persona prompt — plus a lightweight
rating loop so I can mark good/bad responses and have that shape future
behavior. No model training in this ticket.

Context: This is prompt-conditioning, deliberately not fine-tuning. Traits
work through the existing persona-in-prompt pipeline. The rating loop's job
is to grow each trait's few-shot example set from responses I actually
liked, and record rules from ones I didn't.

Scope:
1. Trait data model — {name, behavior_rules[], example_exchanges[]},
   attachable to any character (premade or created). Multiple traits
   compose into one persona prompt in a defined order (backstory, traits,
   examples, memory summary).
2. Character creator integration — pick traits when creating a character;
   also editable on existing characters.
3. Rating capture — an unobtrusive in-conversation way to mark a response
   good/bad. Good → stored as a candidate example line for the active
   trait(s); bad → logged with the response for my later review. Candidates
   go to a review file, NOT auto-promoted into prompts — I curate.
4. Prompt-order check — ensure trait rules are asserted after the memory
   summary in assembly order, so long-conversation drift doesn't dilute
   traits.

   accumulates that a future LoRA fine-tune could use if conditioning
   demonstrably fails.

Goal: NPCs can talk to each other, and the player can form a small group —
ask an NPC to follow you, walk to another NPC, and have a three-way (or
N-way) conversation instead of strictly one-on-one.

Context: Builds on the shared world-fact bus and per-NPC memory. Group
conversation is turn-based over the same structured-JSON dialogue pipeline:
each turn, one participant's persona prompt is assembled (their persona +
traits + their view of relevant facts + the conversation so far) and they
respond. NPC-to-NPC exchanges write facts to the world bus like any other
conversation.

Scope:
1. Follow mechanic — ask an NPC (subject to affinity/persona willingness)
   to follow; simple follow movement.
2. Group conversation state — a participant list instead of a single NPC;
   speaking order resolved simply (round-robin or addressed-by-name);
   player messages can address the group or a named participant.
3. NPC-to-NPC turns — when it's an NPC's turn responding to another NPC,
   same pipeline, with the other NPC's last line as input. Cap consecutive
   NPC-to-NPC turns (e.g. 2–3) before returning to the player so
   conversations don't run away without them.
4. Ambient NPC-to-NPC chatter (two NPCs whose schedules put them together
   exchanging a line or two the player can overhear) — include only if it
   falls out naturally from the group mechanism; otherwise list as
   follow-up, don't force it.
5. Memory/fact writes — each participant's private memory updates from
   their own perspective; shared facts revealed in group conversation go to
   the world bus attributed to whoever said them.

Goal: Describe a map or cast of characters in natural language, and a local
LLM generates it — by emitting a structured spec (the sandbox editor's own
map JSON format, and the character system's persona/trait/look records)
that existing systems render. The LLM never draws or places anything
directly; it fills schemas.

Context: Depends on the sandbox map editor (its save format is the output
contract) and the trait system (its records are the character output
contract). Schema-as-contract, same as NPC dialogue: model proposes a
structured spec, validation layer checks it (valid piece ids, in-bounds
placements, no collision-rule violations), then the normal loaders render
it. A coding-oriented local model (e.g. Ornith) is a reasonable candidate
here since the task is structured-output generation, but benchmark it
against the current dialogue model on schema-validity rate before assuming
— pick by measured validity, not by label.

Scope:
1. Map generation — prompt template that takes my description plus the
   piece catalog (ids, footprints, style tags) and emits a valid map file.
   Validate before loading; on invalid output, retry with the validation
   errors fed back (cap retries, then report failure plainly).
2. Character generation — same pattern emitting persona + traits + look
   records, constrained to existing part ids and trait names.
3. Combined flow — "make me a fishing village with a grumpy old sailor and
   two kids" produces a map with those characters placed in it.
4. In-game entry point — a simple text-input flow in sandbox mode; results
   load as an editable sandbox map, not a locked artifact, so I can fix
   what the model gets wrong by hand.

- No clarifying questions or /grill-me-style interrogation; pick the most
  defensible option, log reasoning, keep going.

  a cloud model first if configured, then confirm on local. Log
  schema-validity rates for whichever local models were tested.
- The validation layer is the deliverable as much as the generation —
  generated output that loads without being validated is a failed ticket
  even if it happens to look right.
- Follow existing CLAUDE.md agent routing. Draft PR only, no merge, no
  main. Standard gitignore rules apply.

/idea "Add statistical rigor to the strategy arena: compute a Deflated Sharpe Ratio for each strategy that accounts for the number of strategies/configurations tested, and require a t-statistic near 3.0 (not the usual 2.0) before a strategy is promoted from backtest to live paper trading. Also switch walk-forward validation to purged/embargoed cross-validation to prevent leakage from overlapping return windows."

/idea "Add a realistic cost model to the backtest and arena comparison that treats bid-ask spread as the dominant cost (not just commission, since Robinhood is $0 commission), scaled by each ticker's typical spread and the position's size relative to average volume. Any strategy whose backtested edge doesn't survive this cost model should be flagged, not just ranked lower."

/idea "Add a post-earnings-announcement drift (PEAD) strategy: after an earnings report, rank stocks by the size of their earnings surprise and go long the top-surprise names, holding for roughly 60-90 days per the academic literature. Needs an earnings-surprise data source (Alpha Vantage or another feed) and should filter to liquid tickers to avoid the small-cap transaction-cost trap the research flagged."

/idea "Add a time-series trend-following strategy per ticker: compute each stock's own trailing return over a 3-12 month lookback and go long only if that trend is positive, no cross-sectional ranking involved. Combine with volatility scaling from the start rather than adding it later, since the research shows this roughly doubles the Sharpe ratio and cuts crash risk."

/idea "Add a low-volatility stock selection strategy: rank the tradeable universe by trailing realized volatility (or beta) and prefer long positions in the lowest-volatility names, as a long-only proxy for the betting-against-beta premium that doesn't require shorting."

/idea "Refactor the existing candlestick pattern and RSI/MACD technical indicator strategies so they no longer trade as standalone strategies in the arena, and instead become input features/confirmation filters that feed the GBM model or gate other strategies' entries. Keep the historical arena results for these as a reference but stop treating them as independent alpha sources, since the research showed weak/contested standalone evidence for candlestick patterns in isolation."

/idea "Add volatility-targeted position sizing across all strategies: scale each position so it targets a constant contribution to portfolio volatility based on the ticker's trailing realized volatility, rather than flat position sizing. This should be the first risk control implemented, ahead of stop-losses or Kelly sizing, per the strongest evidence in the research."

/idea "Add fractional-Kelly position sizing (configurable between quarter-Kelly and half-Kelly) computed from each strategy's estimated edge and variance, capping any single position well below full Kelly to account for estimation error in the edge itself."

/idea "Add ATR-based trailing stop-losses per position, sized to each stock's own volatility rather than a flat percentage, plus a portfolio-level max-drawdown circuit breaker that pauses all live trading once cumulative losses cross a configurable threshold."
